### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.clue

### Question

With `mini.clue` disabled, mappings `go` and `goo` work where `go` triggers after `timeoutlen`. WIth `mini.clue` enabled, mapping `go` does not work (it just shows the clue) regardless of time elapsed. Is it possible to still use both mappings? I assume this behavior is known and I might have glossed over that implication from taking a glimpse at the docs (new to Neovim, not clear on some terminologies).

Contributing guidelines

 I have read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Module(s)
mini.clue
Question
With mini.clue disabled, mappings go and goo work where go triggers after timeoutlen. WIth mini.clue enabled, mapping go does not work (it just shows the clue) regardless of time elapsed. Is it possible to still use both mappings? I assume this behavior is known and I might have glossed over that implication from taking a glimpse at the docs (new to Neovim, not clear on some terminologies).

comment_data.body:
Yes, it is possible if only `g` is mapped as trigger (which is the suggested case).

Executing `go` is possible after typing `go` [followed by `<CR>`](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/15abccbe23525ee0502d2efe620c77db00bfb93c/doc/mini-clue.txt#L16) to execute currently typed keys. The `go` keys will then be emulated as if user pressed it normally, which means waiting another 'timeoutlen' milliseconds and Neovim will execute the mapping behind `go`.

But my honest suggestion is to avoid this situation (to essentially useful mappings where one is the prefix of another) altogether.
